title: Why the Government is About to Shut Down

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是Benjamin Poulin，我是Mark Ronson，欢迎收听《The Reframers》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店里做DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的收藏品去工作，把DJ台变成了一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《The Reframers》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的Michael Barbaro。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《The Daily》。

sentences.en: Today, a showdown between House Republicans and their leader, Speaker Kevin McCarthy, is about to turn into a government shutdown this weekend.
sentences.zh: 今天，众议院共和党人与他们的领袖、议长Kevin McCarthy之间的对峙，即将导致本周末政府停摆。

sentences.en: My colleague, Chief Washington Correspondent Carl Hulse, takes us inside the causes and the consequences of the looming crisis.
sentences.zh: 我的同事、华盛顿首席记者Carl Hulse将带我们深入了解这场迫在眉睫的危机的起因和后果。

sentences.en: It's Friday, September 29th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月29日，星期五。

sentences.en: We are talking to you at about 12 o'clock on Thursday afternoon.
sentences.zh: 我们是在周四下午12点左右与你通话的。

sentences.en: At this very moment, in your estimation, how likely is it that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，在你看来，美国政府停摆的可能性有多大？

sentences.en: government shuts down, the deadline is 12.01 a.m.
sentences.zh: 截止期限是周六凌晨12点01分。

sentences.en: on Saturday?
sentences.zh: 对吗？

sentences.en: I mean, pretty likely.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，可能性相当大。

sentences.en: And here's one good reason for that.
sentences.zh: 原因之一就在这里。

sentences.en: The Senate right now is not even scheduled to take a final vote on its emergency plan until Sunday.
sentences.zh: 参议院目前甚至还没安排在周日之前对紧急方案进行最终投票。

sentences.en: Which is not very helpful when the deadline is midnight Saturday.
sentences.zh: 而截止日期是周六午夜，这显然没什么帮助。

sentences.en: I mean, there could be a kumbaya moment where everyone says, okay, listen, we're going to avoid this.
sentences.zh: 我是说，可能会出现一个大家齐心协力说“好吧，听着，我们要避免这种情况”的时刻。

sentences.en: Let's just pass something to keep the money going.
sentences.zh: 让我们通过一些法案来维持资金运转吧。

sentences.en: Panic could set in.
sentences.zh: 恐慌可能会随之而来。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's like, oh, we're going to get killed for this.
sentences.zh: 就像是，“哦，我们会因为这个被骂死的”。

sentences.en: Let's not do it.
sentences.zh: 我们还是别这么做了。

sentences.en: But right now, the timetable itself is set to have a shutdown.
sentences.zh: 但就目前而言，时间表本身就注定了政府会停摆。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So we want you to explain, in way only you can, why we're going to be enduring this awful experience of a government shutdown, why it is now looking inevitable.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想请你用你特有的方式解释一下，为什么我们要忍受政府停摆这种糟糕的经历，为什么现在看来这已不可避免。

sentences.en: And a lot of the basic dynamics, of course, Carl, have become very familiar to our listeners, that Republicans have a very slender majority.
sentences.zh: 当然，Carl，很多基本动态我们的听众已经很熟悉了，那就是共和党人只有微弱的多数优势。

sentences.en: And ever since they took over the House at the beginning of the year,
sentences.zh: 自从他们年初接管众议院以来，

sentences.en: that has meant that a very tiny group of hard-right conservatives have been able to basically run the United States House of Representatives.
sentences.zh: 这意味着一小群极右翼保守派基本上能够掌控美国众议院。

sentences.en: And Kevin McCarthy.
sentences.zh: 还有Kevin McCarthy。

sentences.en: So I take it back to his election for the Speaker, about 20 very hardcore conservative Republicans at various points in that election were opposed to Speaker McCarthy.
sentences.zh: 回想他竞选议长时，大约20名强硬派保守党共和党人在选举的各个阶段都反对McCarthy议长。

sentences.en: So he couldn't really get elected without making some concessions to these people.
sentences.zh: 所以如果不向这些人做出一些让步，他根本无法当选。

sentences.en: Certainly the Democrats weren't going to bail him out.
sentences.zh: 当然，民主党人是不会帮他的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So he made a lot of promises back then.
sentences.zh: 所以他当时许下了很多承诺。

sentences.en: None of them were written down.
sentences.zh: 没有一条是写下来的。

sentences.en: And all of us have asked, hey, can we see these promises?
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都问过，嘿，能让我们看看这些承诺吗？

sentences.en: And Kevin McCarthy said he didn't want anything written down.
sentences.zh: Kevin McCarthy说他不想把任何东西写下来。

sentences.en: So among those promises was to return federal spending to pre-COVID levels.
sentences.zh: 在这些承诺中，有一项是将联邦支出恢复到疫情前的水平。

sentences.en: That's what conservative Republicans want.
sentences.zh: 这就是保守派共和党人想要的。

sentences.en: You know, all that money went out the door for a lot of COVID prograMs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当时为了很多疫情项目，钱像流水一样花出去了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the promise was to go back to pre-COVID spending.
sentences.zh: 所以承诺是回到疫情前的支出水平。

sentences.en: But that just hasn't happened.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有发生。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And they've been putting the heat on him to fulfill that promise.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在向他施压，要求他兑现承诺。

sentences.en: That's basically what's going on.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是现在发生的事情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That was one of the promises, big spending cuts.
sentences.zh: 那是承诺之一，大幅削减开支。

sentences.en: One of the other promises, and this one did get written down, was that at any single moment
sentences.zh: 另一个承诺，而且这个确实写下来了，那就是在McCarthy担任议长期间的任何时刻，

sentences.en: under McCarthy's speakership, a single House Republican could call for McCarthy to be removed
sentences.zh: 任何一名众议院共和党人都可以要求罢免McCarthy的议长职务，

sentences.en: as Speaker, which further empowered these far-right Republicans, as we've talked about in past episodes, because it gives them a kind of veto power over his entire speakership.
sentences.zh: 这进一步增强了这些极右翼共和党人的权力，正如我们在过去几期节目中所讨论的那样，因为它赋予了他们对他整个议长任期的一种否决权。

sentences.en: And now, as you just established, he has disappointed them in that speakership.
sentences.zh: 而现在，正如你刚才所说，他在议长任期内让他们失望了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So you're referring to what's known as the motion to vacate.
sentences.zh: 所以你指的是所谓的“罢免动议”。

sentences.en: So he lives under this threat, and they could bring it forward.
sentences.zh: 他生活在这种威胁之下，他们随时可能提出动议。

sentences.en: So he operates constantly trying to figure out how to avoid having that motion called on him.
sentences.zh: 所以他一直在努力想办法避免被提出动议。

sentences.en: And as I recall, the first really big time we see that play out is a couple months ago during the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我记得我们第一次真正看到这种情况发生是在几个月前的美国债务上限辩论期间。

sentences.en: debt ceiling debate.
sentences.zh: 我知道这些事情都很混乱且堆积在一起，但那是我们上次面临政府能否运作的巨大危机，当时的问题是我们是否会拖欠债务。

sentences.en: This, I know these all get very confusing and piled up, but that was the last time we faced
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: a giant crisis of whether our government could function, and it was around whether we might default on our debt.
sentences.zh: 那是一件非常严重的事情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 比停摆更严重，对吧？

sentences.en: Which was a serious, very serious thing.
sentences.zh: 违约将是历史上第一次，那将是一场经济危机。

sentences.en: More serious than a shutdown, I would say, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我认为Kevin McCarthy意识到了债务上限之争的利害关系。

sentences.en: Defaulting would have been the first time in history it would have been an economic crisis.
sentences.zh: 我们昨晚通宵工作。

sentences.en: So Kevin McCarthy, I think, recognized what was at stake in the debt limit fight.
sentences.zh: 我们正在做最后的定稿。

sentences.en: So we worked through the night last night.
sentences.zh: 他最终决定了。

sentences.en: We're finalizing.
sentences.zh: 与总统坐下来谈。

sentences.en: And he decided ultimately.
sentences.zh: 我说，让我们共同努力提高债务上限，但要控制支出金额。

sentences.en: Sat down with the president.
sentences.zh: 与拜登总统达成了一项协议，设定了某些支出水平，这让许多极右翼成员感到不满。

sentences.en: I said, let's work together to be able to raise the debt ceiling, but curve the amount of spending.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，当你与两党进行谈判时，你必须与两党合作。

sentences.en: To cut a deal with President Biden that set certain spending levels that dissatisfied a lot of his far-right members.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不是每个人都想要的100%的结果。

sentences.en: We know at any time when you sit and negotiate within two parties that you've got to work with both sides of the aisle.
sentences.zh: 但当你审视时，国家将会……

sentences.en: So it's not 100% of what everybody wants.
sentences.zh: 最终，该协议在众议院以民主党票数多于共和党票数的结果获得通过。

sentences.en: But when you look, the country is going to...
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the deal ultimately passed in the House with more Democratic than Republican votes.
sentences.zh: 因为在那一刻，他基本上选择了国家的财务健康，而不是他与这些随时可能解雇他的极右翼共和党人之间的关系。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because in that moment, he basically chooses the nation's financial health over potentially
sentences.zh: 他们非常不高兴。

sentences.en: his own relationship with these far-right Republicans who can kind of fire him at any moment.
sentences.zh: 我在这个协议中看到的是我来到华盛顿特区以来最大的暴行之一。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 特朗普欠下了数万亿美元的债务。

sentences.en: And they were very unhappy.
sentences.zh: 我们进行了广泛的斗争，旨在赋予国会每一位议员权力，而不是单方面将我们的权力交给议长去谈判一项糟糕的协议。

sentences.en: What I see here in this deal is absolutely one of the biggest abominations since I've been in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 现在，为什么共和党领导人总是告诉我们，明年我们会努力抗争？

sentences.en: Trillions and trillions of dollars in debt for Trump.
sentences.zh: 明年我们是认真的。

sentences.en: We fought extensively to empower each individual member of Congress, not unilaterally give our authority over to the speaker to negotiate a bad deal.
sentences.zh: 那时他们划定了界限，说，听着，除非你们满足我们在支出方面的要求，否则我们不会让众议院的事务继续进行。

sentences.en: Now, how come it is that Republican leaders always tell us, next year we'll fight hard?
sentences.zh: 我们将通过程序性的游击战来做到这一点。

sentences.en: We really mean it next year.
sentences.zh: 他们确实做到了。

sentences.en: And that was when they kind of laid down their marker and said, listen, we are not going to let the business of the House go forward unless you meet our demands on spending.
sentences.zh: 相信我，他们非常有效。

sentences.en: And we're going to do that through procedural guerrilla warfare.
sentences.zh: 正是这种动态导致我们走到了今天这一步，面临着停摆的局面。

sentences.en: And they did do it.
sentences.zh: 你认为政府会停摆吗？

sentences.en: And trust me, they've been very effective.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that dynamic is what's gotten us to this point to where we're facing a shutdown.
sentences.zh: 政府停摆是Kevin McCarthy的错。

sentences.en: Do you believe the government is going to shut down?
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们谈谈这个，因为McCarthy非常清楚，他避免停摆、避免另一场潜在政府灾难的唯一方法，

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 就是像他在债务上限和违约风险问题上所做的那样，通过一项民主党人喜欢、一些温和派共和党人也喜欢的法案。

sentences.en: And it's Kevin McCarthy's fault that the government is going to shut down.
sentences.zh: 但当然，正如我们在这里已经非常明确的那样，这使他面临共和党人试图罢免他议长职务的风险。

sentences.en: Well, let's talk about that because McCarthy very well understands the only way he avoids
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: a shutdown, another potential government catastrophe, is to do what he did when it came to the debt
sentences.zh: 这在目前是一个非常真实的风险，因为佛罗里达州共和党人Matt Gaetz，也就是他目前在共和党内的头号宿敌，已经表示如果McCarthy与民主党人达成协议，他就会提出罢免动议。

sentences.en: ceiling and the risk of default, which is to pass a bill that Democrats like and that some moderate Republicans like.
sentences.zh: 但对Kevin McCarthy来说，这是摆脱困境的唯一途径。

sentences.en: But of course, as we have very well established here, that leaves him exposed to this Republican maneuver of trying to oust him as speaker.
sentences.zh: 他必须在某个时候与Chuck Schumer和Joe Biden达成协议。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没有其他办法。

sentences.en: And that's a very real risk right now because Matt Gaetz, a Republican from Florida who's his chief nemesis right now among Republicans, has said if McCarthy makes a deal with the
sentences.zh: 参议院由民主党控制，拜登总统显然也是民主党人。

sentences.en: Democrats, he will go with the motion to vacate.
sentences.zh: 所以他现在的处境是，他试图至少表现出他在对抗民主党人方面立场坚定。

sentences.en: But for Kevin McCarthy, it's kind of the only way out of this mess.
sentences.zh: 但在某个时候，他必须达成协议。

sentences.en: He has to cut a deal at some point with Chuck Schumer and Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 所以他决定做一些他认为能安抚右翼并可能让他度过难关的事情。

sentences.en: There's no other way to do this.
sentences.zh: 那就是宣布对拜登总统进行弹劾调查。

sentences.en: The Senate is controlled by Democrats and President Biden obviously is a Democrat.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So he is in a position where he is trying to at least appear that he's holding firm against the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 他认为这或许能满足这些人，并基本上在支出问题上给他一些回旋余地。

sentences.en: But at some point he has to make a deal.
sentences.zh: 但并没有。

sentences.en: So he decided to do something that he thought would appease the right and maybe get him past this.
sentences.zh: 他们无论如何都想弹劾总统。

sentences.en: And that was announcing an impeachment inquiry of President Biden.
sentences.zh: 而财政鹰派则认为，这并不能改变我们在支出问题上的想法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 我们仍然想要这些削减开支的措施，即使许多更主流的众议院共和党人并不想要。

sentences.en: He thought that could maybe satisfy these guys and give him some wiggle room on spending, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这种内部纠纷真的把事情搞砸了，用一个专业术语来说。

sentences.en: But it didn't.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使是对美国总统进行弹劾调查，基于我们已经确定的相当站不住脚的证据，也无法为McCarthy从这些极右翼共和党人那里赢得足够的善意，从而避免我们冲向停摆。

sentences.en: They wanted to impeach the president anyway.
sentences.zh: 我只是想了解为什么McCarthy不能再次与民主党人合作来拯救这个系统，并假设如果他这样做，那些民主党人可能会在极右翼共和党人想要进行的最终罢免投票中帮他一把。

sentences.en: And the fiscal hawks are like, well, that doesn't change our mind on spending.
sentences.zh: 这看起来像是一个合理的政治算计。

sentences.en: We still want these spending cuts that even a lot of the more mainstream House Republicans don't want.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, you know, this internal dispute has really messed things up, to use a technical term.
sentences.zh: 嗯，Michael，我不认为这有多合理。

sentences.en: So not even an impeachment inquiry into the president of the United States, based on what we have established as pretty shaky evidence, is able to buy McCarthy enough goodwill with
sentences.zh: 所以，如果他与民主党人达成协议，肯定会有人采取行动罢免他。

sentences.en: these hard-right Republicans to avoid us hurtling towards a shutdown.
sentences.zh: 每个人都承诺过这一点。

sentences.en: I just want to understand why McCarthy cannot once again work with the Democrats to save the system and perhaps assume that if he does that, those Democrats might bail him out in
sentences.zh: McCarthy知道这一点。

sentences.en: an eventual vote that the far-right Republicans might want to hold to oust him.
sentences.zh: 所以，你的问题是，民主党人会来救援吗？

sentences.en: That would seem like a reasonable political calculation.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我曾就此与多位民主党人交谈过，包括就在昨天，民主党领袖Hakeem Jeffries，当然是来自纽约的那位。

sentences.en: Well, I don't think it's all that reasonable, Michael.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们还没到那一步。

sentences.en: So, if he makes a deal with the Democrats, there's certainly going to be a move to oust him.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至还没考虑过这个问题。

sentences.en: Everyone has promised that.
sentences.zh: 我不确定他们是否真的没考虑过。

sentences.en: McCarthy knows that.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们考虑了很多。

sentences.en: So, your question is, are the Democrats going to ride to the rescue?
sentences.zh: 他们只是没说出来，当然也没对我提起。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 但是，我认为在债务上限投票后，民主党人对McCarthy是满意的。

sentences.en: I have talked to numerous Democrats about this, including the Democratic leader just yesterday,
sentences.zh: 他愿意承担风险。

sentences.en: Hakeem Jeffries, from New York, obviously.
sentences.zh: 他挽救了国家的财务状况、信用评级以及我们所有的401k退休金，对吧？

sentences.en: He says, we're not there yet.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We're not even thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想如果当时进行那次投票，他可能会得到民主党人的帮助。

sentences.en: I'm not sure they're not even thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 现在，我不确定他还能不能得到民主党人的任何帮助，因为他为了安抚极右翼做了什么？

sentences.en: I think they're thinking a lot about it.
sentences.zh: 第一，他没有坚持他达成的债务上限协议。

sentences.en: They're just not talking about it, and certainly not to me.
sentences.zh: 第二，他说，让我们弹劾Joe Biden吧。

sentences.en: But, I think after the debt limit vote, the Democrats were happy with McCarthy.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们会想，我们为什么要支持这家伙？

sentences.en: He was willing to take the risk.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He saved the country's financial standing and credit rating and all of our 401ks, right?
sentences.zh: 这些并不是获得民主党支持的关键，背弃协议并启动一个可能罢免他们总统的程序。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, I think if they'd have had that vote then, I think he probably would have gotten help from Democrats.
sentences.zh: 所以，显然没有确定性说民主党人会帮助他。

sentences.en: Right now, I'm not sure he gets any help from Democrats, because what did he do to appease the far right?
sentences.zh: 但是，天哪，Kevin McCarthy是多么想当议长啊。

sentences.en: One, he didn't stick to the agreement on the debt limit that he made.
sentences.zh: 他热爱当议长。

sentences.en: And two, he said, let's impeach Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 第二，他说，我们要弹劾乔·拜登。

sentences.en: So, they're like, well, why would we go with this guy?
sentences.zh: 所以他们会想，我们为什么要支持这家伙呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.

sentences.en: Those are not the keys to unlocking Democratic support, bailing out on an agreement and starting a process that could remove their president.
sentences.zh: 撕毁协议并启动可能罢免总统的程序，这些可不是争取民主党支持的良策。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.

sentences.en: So, there is no certainty, obviously, that Democrats would help him.
sentences.zh: 所以，很显然，民主党人是否会帮他还是个未知数。

sentences.en: But, boy, does Kevin McCarthy want to be Speaker.
sentences.zh: 但是，天哪，凯文·麦卡锡是多么想当议长啊。

sentences.en: He loves being Speaker.
sentences.zh: 他热爱当议长这份工作。

sentences.en: I've never seen a Speaker, and I think I counted, I've been around for eight, I've never seen anyone kind of relish the job so much.
sentences.zh: 我从未见过哪位议长像他这样，我算了一下，我经历过八位议长，从未见过有人如此沉迷于这份工作。

sentences.en: He stands in the rotunda in a photo line and shakes hands and takes selfies with tourists.
sentences.zh: 他站在圆形大厅的拍照队列里，与游客握手、自拍。

sentences.en: I mean, the guy is really into it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这家伙真的很享受。

sentences.en: So, he does not want to lose that job, certainly in, like, an embarrassing, humiliating thing on the floor.
sentences.zh: 所以，他不想失去这份工作，尤其是不想在众议院大厅里以一种尴尬、丢脸的方式失去它。

sentences.en: And you remember, we were all standing there watching these 15 votes that it took for him to become Speaker, most people, I think, would have said, I don't really want it that bad.
sentences.zh: 你还记得，我们当时都站在那里看着他经过15轮投票才当选议长，我想大多数人都会说，我可没那么想要这个职位。

sentences.en: But he did.
sentences.zh: 但他想要。

sentences.en: And he does.
sentences.zh: 而且他现在依然想要。

sentences.en: So, Carl, what I'm hearing you say is we should not underestimate the degree to which Kevin
sentences.zh: 所以，卡尔，我听你的意思是，我们不应低估凯文·麦卡锡

sentences.en: McCarthy will cling to this job with everything he has to the very last possible minute because he just wants desperately to stay on his Speaker.
sentences.zh: 会竭尽全力死守这个职位的程度，直到最后一刻，因为他太渴望保住议长的位置了。

sentences.en: And so, this shutdown will be the exact opposite dynamic of what happened with that debt ceiling negotiation.
sentences.zh: 因此，这次政府停摆的态势将与之前的债务上限谈判完全相反。

sentences.en: Instead of being willing to risk his job to save the system, McCarthy will pretty consciously sacrifice the system to save this job he loves so much.
sentences.zh: 麦卡锡不会为了拯救体制而甘冒丢掉工作的风险，而是会相当清醒地牺牲体制来保住他如此钟爱的工作。

sentences.en: We don't know yet what his moment of truth is going to be.
sentences.zh: 我们还不知道他的“关键时刻”何时到来。

sentences.en: He could still capitulate here and say, OK, I've got to do something to keep the government open.
sentences.zh: 他仍然可能在这里妥协，说：好吧，我必须做点什么来维持政府运转。

sentences.en: I'm going to work with Democrats.
sentences.zh: 我要和民主党人合作。

sentences.en: I'm going to take the risk.
sentences.zh: 我要承担这个风险。

sentences.en: I'm a little Irish, OK?
sentences.zh: 我身上有点爱尔兰人的倔强，好吗？

sentences.en: I don't walk away from a battle.
sentences.zh: 我不会临阵脱逃。

sentences.en: I knew changing Washington would not be easy.
sentences.zh: 我知道改变华盛顿绝非易事。

sentences.en: But so far, we have not seen that as he did in the debt limit.
sentences.zh: 但到目前为止，我们还没看到他像处理债务上限那样采取行动。

sentences.en: We want to be able to win the policies that we've been fighting for and telling the American public.
sentences.zh: 我们希望能够赢得我们一直在争取并向美国公众承诺的政策。

sentences.en: And I think right now, he is putting his interest in that job ahead of the possible consequences of a shutdown, which we are, at this very moment, careening towards.
sentences.zh: 我认为此刻，他将自己对职位的私利置于政府停摆可能带来的后果之上，而我们此刻正冲向那个深渊。

sentences.en: And you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: If it takes a fight, I'll have a fight.
sentences.zh: 如果非要一战，那我就奉陪到底。

sentences.en: And it's going to have big consequences.
sentences.zh: 这将会带来严重的后果。

sentences.en: We've been through this before.
sentences.zh: 我们以前经历过这种情况。

sentences.en: And we know that there is some pain.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这会带来一些痛苦。

sentences.en: Some real pain.
sentences.zh: 一些真正的痛苦。

sentences.en: Some real pain for people.
sentences.zh: 给人们带来真正的痛苦。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝创刊175周年。

sentences.en: So Carl, I want to talk about the pain that comes with a shutdown, assuming, as we are now doing, that there's going to be a shutdown in the next day or two.
sentences.zh: 卡尔，我想谈谈政府停摆带来的痛苦，假设我们现在认为未来一两天内就会发生停摆。

sentences.en: And this is not, of course, your first shutdown.
sentences.zh: 当然，这也不是你第一次经历政府停摆了。

sentences.en: So you bring some real authority to the subject of this pain.
sentences.zh: 所以你在谈论这种痛苦时很有发言权。

sentences.en: Not my first shutdown rodeo, as they say.
sentences.zh: 正如他们所说，这已经不是我第一次经历停摆了。

sentences.en: I can't tell you how many I've been through, but I've been through long ones, short ones, medium ones.
sentences.zh: 我数不清经历过多少次了，有长的、短的，还有中等长度的。

sentences.en: They all have their own little dynamic.
sentences.zh: 它们都有各自的特点。

sentences.en: This one's a little different because past shutdowns have been like over one big issue, right?
sentences.zh: 这次有点不同，因为过去的停摆通常围绕一个重大议题，对吧？

sentences.en: So over Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 比如围绕奥巴马医改。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That was a shutdown.
sentences.zh: 那是一次停摆。

sentences.en: The Democrats forced a very brief shutdown in 2018 over DACA, the young undocumented immigrants brought here as kids and whether to get them citizenship.
sentences.zh: 2018年，民主党人因“童年抵美者暂缓遣返计划”（DACA）——即那些从小被带到这里的无证移民是否应获得公民身份的问题——引发了一次短暂的停摆。

sentences.en: Trump had one over the border wall.
sentences.zh: 特朗普时期则是因为边境墙问题。

sentences.en: This is a little more amorphous.
sentences.zh: 这次的情况比较模糊。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But the government, unfortunately, knows how to do this.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，政府知道该怎么应对。

sentences.en: There's a manual.
sentences.zh: 有一本手册。

sentences.en: Literally a manual.
sentences.zh: 确实有一本手册。

sentences.en: I'm sure there's many, many manuals, actually.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定，实际上有很多很多手册。

sentences.en: But if this one happens, it's going to happen on the weekend.
sentences.zh: 但如果这次停摆发生，它会发生在周末。

sentences.en: So the first consequences won't be felt as much.
sentences.zh: 所以最初的后果不会那么明显。

sentences.en: It'll be kind of like a slow rolling disaster if it goes into next week.
sentences.zh: 如果持续到下周，那就像一场缓慢推进的灾难。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of things that happen.
sentences.zh: 会有很多事情发生。

sentences.en: And certainly things stay open.
sentences.zh: 当然，有些部门会保持开放。

sentences.en: There's essential people, but they won't be paid.
sentences.zh: 会有必要岗位的人员留守，但他们拿不到工资。

sentences.en: I have a son who works on Capitol Hill, and he is not relishing the prospect of not being paid.
sentences.zh: 我儿子在国会山工作，他可不想面对拿不到工资的前景。

sentences.en: Certainly in Washington and the surrounding area, there's a lot of people who will be going without paychecks if this goes for very long.
sentences.zh: 当然，在华盛顿及周边地区，如果这种情况持续太久，很多人将失去收入来源。

sentences.en: The military will not be paid.
sentences.zh: 军人将拿不到工资。

sentences.en: In the past, that's been avoided either through a special bill to make sure that they keep getting paid, or the defense spending bill had already been passed.
sentences.zh: 过去，这种情况要么通过特别法案确保他们继续领薪，要么国防支出法案已经获得通过，从而避免了这个问题。

sentences.en: So that part of the government was covered.
sentences.zh: 所以政府的那部分得到了保障。

sentences.en: This time, not the case.
sentences.zh: 这次情况不同。

sentences.en: So they wouldn't be paid unless there's a special step taken to pay them.
sentences.zh: 所以除非采取特别措施支付工资，否则他们拿不到钱。

sentences.en: That has not happened so far.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止还没有发生这种情况。

sentences.en: Another really important group that won't be paid are air traffic controllers.
sentences.zh: 另一个拿不到工资的重要群体是空中交通管制员。

sentences.en: Obviously, hugely important to the economy and just to life in general, right?
sentences.zh: 显然，这对经济乃至日常生活都至关重要，对吧？

sentences.en: We've already seen a bunch of travel disruptions over the past months.
sentences.zh: 过去几个月我们已经看到了大量的旅行中断。

sentences.en: So can you imagine what happens if there's some sort of slowdown there with air traffic controllers?
sentences.zh: 所以你能想象如果空中交通管制出现某种放缓会发生什么吗？

sentences.en: I mean, how long are they going to be willing to work without paid?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们愿意在没有报酬的情况下工作多久？

sentences.en: It's like, these jobs are stressful enough.
sentences.zh: 这些工作本身压力就够大了。

sentences.en: Do you really want them being more stressed out by their economic worries?
sentences.zh: 你真的希望他们因为经济担忧而承受更大的压力吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I guess we should add, Carl, as our colleagues have reported in the Times, that there's a longtime national shortage of air traffic controllers.
sentences.zh: 我想我们应该补充一点，卡尔，正如我们在《时报》的同事所报道的那样，全国范围内长期存在空中交通管制员短缺的问题。

sentences.en: It's well documented.
sentences.zh: 这是有据可查的。

sentences.en: And the idea of not paying controllers, as you've just raised, might lead some controllers to not show up at work, maybe call in sick.
sentences.zh: 正如你刚才提到的，不给管制员发工资的想法，可能会导致一些管制员不再上班，甚至请病假。

sentences.en: And then you've got, you know, thousands of planes in the airs and not enough air traffic controllers.
sentences.zh: 到时候天上有成千上万架飞机，却缺乏足够的空中交通管制员。

sentences.en: And that's an incredibly dangerous situation.
sentences.zh: 那将是一个极其危险的局面。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm not looking forward to catching a plane in those circumstances, but I think that this is a real concern that people have.
sentences.zh: 是的，在这种情况下我可不想坐飞机，但我认为这是人们真正担心的问题。

sentences.en: What will happen to the air traffic control system?
sentences.zh: 空中交通管制系统会发生什么？

sentences.en: What happens to the airports?
sentences.zh: 机场会发生什么？

sentences.en: Also, I mean, air traffic controllers, obviously, aren't the only thing.
sentences.zh: 而且，空中交通管制员显然不是唯一受影响的。

sentences.en: There's other big popular parts of the federal government that will be affected.
sentences.zh: 联邦政府还有其他广受欢迎的重要部门也会受到影响。

sentences.en: National parks.
sentences.zh: 国家公园。

sentences.en: Now, you still may be able to go into a national park, but there's not going to be any like facilities open, bathrooms even.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能还能进入国家公园，但不会有任何设施开放，甚至连厕所都没有。

sentences.en: And, you know, one of the big images from past shutdowns is trash piling up out on the
sentences.zh: 你知道，过去停摆时的一个典型画面就是垃圾在国家广场上堆积如山。

sentences.en: National Mall.
sentences.zh: 国家广场。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because the people who would normally pick it up aren't being paid.
sentences.zh: 因为平时负责清理的人拿不到工资。

sentences.en: They're not working.
sentences.zh: 他们没在工作。

sentences.en: Are not there.
sentences.zh: 他们不在那里。

sentences.en: And the government also like prohibits volunteers from my recollection is you can't go out there and pick up that trash.
sentences.zh: 据我记忆，政府还禁止志愿者去清理那些垃圾。

sentences.en: So the consequences of this and the reach of it are very broad.
sentences.zh: 所以这次停摆的后果和影响范围非常广泛。

sentences.en: And here's another thing.
sentences.zh: 还有一件事。

sentences.en: It costs billions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 这会耗费数十亿美元。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: There's all sorts of costs associated with the shutdown, you know, shutting things down, starting them back up.
sentences.zh: 与停摆相关的所有成本，你知道，关闭设施、重新启动等等。

sentences.en: I mean, the federal government is a huge thing.
sentences.zh: 联邦政府是一个庞大的机构。

sentences.en: And so you don't just go, OK, it stops, you know, then you got to restart everything.
sentences.zh: 所以你不能只是说“好吧，它停了”，然后你还得重启一切。

sentences.en: So there is an actual economic cost here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里存在实际的经济成本。

sentences.en: That, of course, Carl, is a bit ironic for the people who are triggering this shutdown, who say that they want to cut federal spending.
sentences.zh: 卡尔，对于那些引发这次停摆、声称要削减联邦支出的人来说，这当然有点讽刺。

sentences.en: You're saying on some level, this is going to cost the government more money.
sentences.zh: 你是说在某种程度上，这反而会让政府花更多的钱。

sentences.en: Yes, definitely true.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是真的。

sentences.en: I mean, there are costs associated with it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这确实伴随着成本。

sentences.en: And that is one of the great ironies here, right?
sentences.zh: 这也是这里最大的讽刺之一，对吧？

sentences.en: Also interesting, lawmakers get paid because of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 还有一点很有趣，根据宪法，议员们照样领工资。

sentences.en: So they can't stop themselves from being paid, which is also sort of not a great look for them.
sentences.zh: 所以他们无法阻止自己领薪水，这看起来对他们来说也不是什么光彩的事。

sentences.en: No, not a great look when the military is not being paid and air traffic controllers aren't being paid.
sentences.zh: 是的，当军人和空中交通管制员都拿不到工资时，这确实很难看。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So given your experience with past shutdowns, help us understand how, when, and why these things become intolerable at some point, because they always do come to an end.
sentences.zh: 鉴于你对过去停摆的经验，帮我们理解一下，这些事情在什么时候、以何种方式、为何会变得无法忍受，因为它们最终总是会结束的。

sentences.en: There's just a question of how long.
sentences.zh: 问题只是持续多久而已。

sentences.en: I think the last one was around 40 days.
sentences.zh: 我想上一次大约持续了40天。

sentences.en: Yeah, and they do end.
sentences.zh: 是的，它们确实会结束。

sentences.en: And one kind of truism about it is once you get into a shutdown, it gets hard to get out legislatively, right?
sentences.zh: 关于这一点的一个公理是，一旦进入停摆状态，立法上就很难走出来，对吧？

sentences.en: People get dug in, and some people are going to go, oh, it's not that bad.
sentences.zh: 人们会固执己见，有些人会说，哦，没那么糟糕。

sentences.en: But there will be bad.
sentences.zh: 但情况终究会变糟。

sentences.en: I mean, a travel disruption.
sentences.zh: 比如旅行中断。

sentences.en: There'll be something that people will find intolerable as it drags on it.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，总会有一些事情让人们觉得无法忍受。

sentences.en: And generally, just people looking at Congress going, what is wrong with you people?
sentences.zh: 通常人们看着国会会想：你们这些人到底怎么了？

sentences.en: Honestly, I do think that that's a factor.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我认为这也是一个因素。

sentences.en: Right, and in terms of people being mad at Congress and looking at them and saying, what's the matter with you,
sentences.zh: 没错，就人们对国会感到愤怒并看着他们说“你们到底怎么了”而言，

sentences.en: it doesn't feel like the blame here is going to end up being all that ambiguous, right?
sentences.zh: 这里的责任归属似乎并不那么模糊，对吧？

sentences.en: This is a Republican shutdown through and through, and so ultimately it's going to be Republicans who are going to have to decide it's reached a tipping point.
sentences.zh: 这是一场彻头彻尾的共和党停摆，所以最终将是共和党人必须决定是否已经到了临界点。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is really falling hard on the House Republicans, and I think that's a real concern for them going into the election next year,
sentences.zh: 这确实给众议院共和党人带来了沉重压力，我认为这对他们明年的选举来说是一个真正的担忧，

sentences.en: that people are going to go, you know, this is ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 人们会说，这太荒谬了。

sentences.en: Now, you know, they're trying their best to wiggle out of it.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们正竭尽全力想摆脱干系。

sentences.en: McCarthy was asked the other day, he's like, you know, why are we having this shutdown?
sentences.zh: 麦卡锡前几天被问到，为什么会发生这次停摆？

sentences.en: He said, ask Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 他说，去问乔·拜登。

sentences.en: McCarthy is trying to shift the blame right now, but I don't think it's going to work.
sentences.zh: 麦卡锡现在正试图推卸责任，但我认为这行不通。

sentences.en: The House Republicans are going to bear the brunt for this one.
sentences.zh: 众议院共和党人将承担这次停摆的主要后果。

sentences.en: And does that mean that Democrats on some level are over in the corner with a little bit of glee on their faces,
sentences.zh: 那是否意味着民主党人在某种程度上正躲在角落里暗自窃喜，

sentences.en: or do they worry that, like, as with all disasters, it splashes on them too?
sentences.zh: 还是他们担心像所有灾难一样，这也会波及到他们自己？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think a little bit of that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想有一点这种成分。

sentences.en: But I think generally speaking, most people on Capitol Hill are like, we can't do this.
sentences.zh: 但我认为总的来说，国会山的大多数人都觉得，我们不能这样做。

sentences.en: This is horribly disruptive.
sentences.zh: 这太具有破坏性了。

sentences.en: But I think at the White House also, it's like people ultimately look at this and say, well, the president's got to do something.
sentences.zh: 但我认为白宫方面也觉得，人们最终会看着这一切说，总统必须做点什么。

sentences.en: So I think that they are fairly sure that Kevin McCarthy and the Republicans are going to take the hit for this,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他们相当确定凯文·麦卡锡和共和党人会为此买单，

sentences.en: but they don't want it to go on for too long because then people start to say, why aren't you fixing this?
sentences.zh: 但他们也不希望停摆持续太久，因为那样人们就会开始问，为什么你们不解决这个问题？

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So it's a complicated little balancing act for the Democrats and for Biden.
sentences.zh: 所以这对民主党人和拜登来说是一个复杂的平衡游戏。

sentences.en: Carl, as you said earlier, when a deal finally comes, and it always does come, it will, by definition, have to be bipartisan.
sentences.zh: 卡尔，正如你之前所说，当协议最终达成时——它总是会达成的——它在定义上必须是两党合作的结果。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's no way for it not to be.
sentences.zh: 是的，不可能不是这样。

sentences.en: That's what the debt limit showed.
sentences.zh: 债务上限谈判已经证明了这一点。

sentences.en: You have to have a bipartisan solution.
sentences.zh: 你必须有一个两党共同的解决方案。

sentences.en: Chuck Schumer's been saying for weeks, and even Mitch McConnell saying for weeks, has to be bipartisan.
sentences.zh: 查克·舒默几周来一直这么说，甚至米奇·麦康奈尔几周来也一直在说，必须是两党合作。

sentences.en: So it's going to have to be that.
sentences.zh: 所以必须是这样。

sentences.en: And then at that point, we'll see how bad it is for Kevin McCarthy.
sentences.zh: 到那时，我们就会看到这对凯文·麦卡锡来说有多糟糕。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And again, almost by definition, it will be bad for Kevin McCarthy.
sentences.zh: 而且再次强调，几乎可以肯定，这对凯文·麦卡锡来说将是糟糕的。

sentences.en: And then he will have only delayed this inevitable showdown that he fears so much that could endanger this job he loves so much.
sentences.zh: 到那时，他只是推迟了那场他如此恐惧的、可能危及他如此钟爱职位的必然对决。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, all of that's being discussed is only a temporary solution.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，目前讨论的所有方案都只是临时性的。

sentences.en: The most viable resolution of this now being discussed is in the Senate with both Republican and Democratic support.
sentences.zh: 目前讨论出的最可行的解决方案，是在参议院得到了共和党和民主党双方的支持。

sentences.en: But even that one only funds the government through November 17th.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，该方案也只能维持政府运作到11月17日。

sentences.en: So, you know, we're going to be having this fight.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们还得继续这场争斗。

sentences.en: Again, you're saying we're going to be having this fight again.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，你是说我们还得再经历一次这样的争斗。

sentences.en: Again.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Maybe multiple times, actually.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能还不止一次。

sentences.en: So the showdown for Kevin McCarthy is coming.
sentences.zh: 所以凯文·麦卡锡的摊牌时刻即将到来。

sentences.en: The only question is, when does it come and does he survive it?
sentences.zh: 唯一的问题是，这什么时候会发生，他能挺过去吗？

sentences.en: Well, Carl, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，卡尔，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: I assume we will be speaking with you again at some point in the next week.
sentences.zh: 我想下周某个时候我们还会再找你聊聊。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, that's probably true.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，这很可能是真的。

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, I think this is going to be a persistent issue.
sentences.zh: 我是说，是的，我认为这将是一个持续存在的问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, Carl, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，卡尔，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，迈克尔。

sentences.zh: 周四下午，在我们与卡尔交谈后，美国

sentences.en: government began to formally notify federal workers that a government shutdown now appears to be imminent.
sentences.zh: 政府开始正式通知联邦工作人员，政府停摆似乎已迫在眉睫。

sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I do not believe that the current evidence would support articles of impeachment.
sentences.zh: 我不认为目前的证据足以支持弹劾条款。

sentences.en: That is something that an inquiry has to establish.
sentences.zh: 那是调查必须确定的事情。

sentences.en: On Thursday, during the first hearing of House Republicans' impeachment inquiry into President Biden,
sentences.zh: 周四，在众议院共和党人针对拜登总统的弹劾调查首次听证会上，

sentences.en: the star witnesses testified that Republicans lacked proof that Biden has committed impeachable offenses.
sentences.zh: 明星证人作证称，共和党人缺乏证据证明拜登犯下了可弹劾的罪行。

sentences.en: I am not here today to even suggest that there was corruption, fraud, or any wrongdoing.
sentences.zh: 我今天来这里甚至不是为了暗示存在腐败、欺诈或任何不当行为。

sentences.en: In my opinion, more information needs to be gathered and assessed before I would make such an assessment.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，在做出此类评估之前，需要收集和评估更多的信息。

sentences.en: House Republicans are seeking to show that Biden is improperly linked to his son's overseas business dealings, but have struggled to find such evidence.
sentences.zh: 众议院共和党人试图证明拜登与其儿子的海外商业往来有不正当联系，但一直难以找到相关证据。

sentences.en: That prompted a Democrat involved in the hearing, Representative Jamie Raskin, to mock the proceeding as a waste of time.
sentences.zh: 这促使参与听证会的民主党众议员杰米·拉斯金嘲讽这次会议是在浪费时间。

sentences.en: If the Republicans had a smoking gun, or even a dripping water pistol, they would be presenting it today, but they've got nothing on Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 如果共和党人有确凿的证据，哪怕是一把滴水的水枪，他们今天也会拿出来，但他们对乔·拜登一无所获。
